chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Isma'il ibn Jabr who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who looked at a woman, so she fascinated him. So he asked about her, and it was said that she is the daughter of so-and-so. So he went to her father and said, 'Marry me your daughter.' But he married someone else to him, and she gave birth from him. So he came to know that it was not his daughter, and that she is a slave. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The mother is returned to her master, and the child is for the man, and upon the one who married her to him is the value of the child's price to be given to the masters of the mother, as he deceived the man and cheated him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a father deceives a suitor by marrying his slave daughter as if she were free?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *gharar* (deception) in marriage contracts, specifically regarding the status of the wife's lineage and freedom. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that while the child follows the father, the slave mother reverts to her master, and the deceiving father bears the financial liability by compensating the master for the child's value, reflecting the loss of the child's potential future service or status. This ruling underscores the importance of transparency in marital negotiations within Shia jurisprudence.
